blocks.heading: Phiano
blocks.subtitle: A word has no position — only its relations.
blocks.body: Phiano reads a story as a forest of trees. Tell it something, and it finds where the sentence belongs, what each word keeps company with, which words are new, and how the whole thing divides. Nothing is a point; everything is a relation under a condition.

blocks.lead: The story the system was told:

forest.title: The forest
forest.sub: Two roots, and a story cast down one of them.

blocks.caption: The scope tree is a bounding-volume hierarchy whose node holds a distribution, not a box. Six words of the story are cast from the roots down; the hit test is the movement in nats, the pruning is the beam.

A real bounding-volume hierarchy, and the same walk over conditions: the volume is what a scope says, 'contains' is a scope saying what its subtree says, and a miss means the reading falls back to the language's.

trees.title: The sixteen trees
trees.sub: And where a bounding-volume hierarchy sits among them.

blocks.caption: Every tree the system holds names a node, a child relation, and a ray. The bounding-volume hierarchy is number 1: the volume is a distribution, the hit test D4's movement in nats.

items.title: 1 · the scope tree
items.body: node: a scope: a text, a chapter, a paragraph — a word too, since a kind and a condition are words  ·  ray: a few words and their pairs, cast from the roots down, entering only children that say them more than the whole tree does

items.title: 2 · the text tree
items.body: node: a directory, a `.txt` file, a blank-line paragraph  ·  ray: reading a text builds it; nothing is queried, it is the tree the scope tree is told from

items.title: 3 · the strand's cut tree
items.body: node: a span of tokens, `start..end`  ·  ray: none: the tree is built once, then read at sixty-four resolutions

items.title: 4 · the sixty-four levels
items.body: node: a unit of one level, `AAA` (the word) to `TTT` (the whole story)  ·  ray: a word asked at a level reads the unit holding it

items.title: 5 · the reading path
items.body: node: a unit on the path from the word up to the whole story  ·  ray: the word being read; its ancestors are mixed, weights counted for it

items.title: 6 · the tree of knowing's levels
items.body: node: a condition: a scope, the last word, the last pair, or a word under a scope  ·  ray: the words said so far; what the levels give is the next word's distribution

items.title: 7 · the condition tree (X ⇒ Y under c)
items.body: node: a word, and a condition which is itself a word  ·  ray: a word plus the condition it is read under

items.title: 8 · the quest's walk
items.body: node: a word asked of the oracle  ·  ray: the frontier: the quest walks outward from the seed

items.title: 9 · the code tree
items.body: node: a crate, a module, a function, a token of its body  ·  ray: a function's words, cast to find where a new function belongs

items.title: 10 · the kin tree
items.body: node: a word  ·  ray: a word never told after the last one; its kin answer in its place

items.title: 11 · the phasor's channels
items.body: node: a word  ·  ray: two words compared on a channel (agreement) or over all of them (resonance)

items.title: 12 · the helix
items.body: node: a directory of the facet's tree, coded as a codon  ·  ray: `ls`, `grep`, `cat` — the file system is the query language

items.title: 13 · the sphere's degrees
items.body: node: a degree `l` of the spherical harmonics  ·  ray: a word read at a lower degree is the word at a coarser resolution

items.title: 14 · the operator's tape
items.body: node: a value on the autograd tape  ·  ray: the backward pass walks it from the loss

items.title: 15 · the Fourier modes
items.body: node: a mode of the operator's spectral weight  ·  ray: a function passed through: low modes carry it, high modes must earn their place

items.title: 16 · the forest
items.body: node: a whole told text with its own root  ·  ray: a story cast into every root at once; the one that says it most holds it

blocks.caption: The story divided without being told where its parts are: TTT is one unit, and each level below it is the story told in more, smaller beats, each beat in the words it says beyond the beat above.

blocks.lead: Nothing is generated; every word of every level is the story's own. The division is made on the information each cut gains against the prior, so the words that carry each beat are the ones that carry the most meaning there.

words.title: A word's company
words.sub: What the forest holds of each word.

blocks.caption: How often the language had heard each word, the post (how hard the word moves the next-word answer), and the words it never heard at all.

blocks.title: Every word (heard · post · next in Emma · kin)

unheard.title: The words it never heard
unheard.sub: Reading a slot from both sides.

blocks.caption: Sixteen words of the story Emma never heard. The system does not know what 'threshold' means; it knows the shape of the hole — the best word between 'has exceeded the' and 'of' is rest, idea, sort.

blocks.title: The slot, read from both sides

blocks.lead: This is the frontier, not a solved problem. Where a word was never told after the last, nothing yet beats plain frequency — the paradigm's hardest claim, a relation reached through what else is known.

world.title: A word has no position
world.sub: The story as a field of phasors.

blocks.caption: Told to a phiecs world, a word is an entity with no coordinate — only angles on up to 64 relation channels. To relate two words is to move them toward each other on one channel.

blocks.title: Who ends up near whom (the cosine over every channel both moved)

readers.title: Reading forward and back
readers.sub: The trained operators on a new story.

blocks.caption: Each learned reader is a matched filter over the relation circle. It reads the next word forward, and — by the conjugate filter, never trained for it — the word that came before.

blocks.title: Operators trained on Emma alone, read on this story

blocks.lead: A reader trained on one author reads a new, misspelt, capitalised story poorly — and that is the honest, expected result. On held-out Emma the same FNO reads the next word first about 18% of the time. Phase carries the whole reading: amplitude alone reads almost nothing.

understood.title: Have we understood language?
understood.sub: What the forest shows, and what it does not.

blocks.lead: A told story enters the structures already there, and each one gives a checkable reading: where it belongs, what its words keep company with, which words are new, what fills their place, how it divides, how it reads forward and back.

sections.title: What it does
sections.body: It learns from one telling, keeps every relation so you can read it, and places a sentence in a structure counted from use alone.

sections.title: What it does not
sections.body: The casts are drawn by function words, not by sense. The trained readers get about 6 of 84 next words first on unfamiliar vocabulary. Where a word was never told after the last, nothing yet beats frequency.

sections.title: The verdict
sections.body: This is not a proof of understanding but an apparatus in which a sentence has a place, a word has company, and both are counted — meaning-as-use made into a measured structure, which is the claim the apparatus tests, not the verdict it returns.
